newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS - Dresdner funds move aims for global status.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Dresdner funds move aims for global status.

text.p: Germany's Dresdner Bank AG on Friday revealed plans to merge its foreign institutional funds business under one roof, pushing forward its aim to become a global player in asset management.

Led by the bank's newly-acquired U.S. unit RCM Capital Management, the division will also bring in the institutional funds business of London's Kleinwort Benson International Management and the smaller Thornton & Co, active in Asia.

The unit, whose name and launch date are not yet finalised, will have 900 staff worldwide and assets under management of more than $50 billion, a quarter of the $200 billion managed asset volume of the whole Dresdner group.
Analysts welcomed the move, saying it made sense to give a management role to RCM, which is viewed as having the highest level of funds expertise in the Dresdner group.

The move was also viewed as confirming the controversial trend among German banks to focus investment banking abroad, which has exposed them to charges of undermining the country's aim to be a leading European financial centre.
"Germany is not where it's at in investment banking. If you want to be a global investment bank, you don't do it from Frankfurt," remarked Merck Finck analyst Konrad Becker.

Dresdner, Germany's second largest commercial bank, said the new unit would spearhead the ambitions it shares with larger rival Deutsche Bank AG and other leading German banks to become a global asset management player.
"There is an extremely complementary fit between these organisations," board member Gerhard Eberstadt said in a statement released in Frankfurt, London and New York.
"The integration of these businesses will bring enormous advantages to clients worldwide, bringing together a broad and enhanced range of global investment products," he said.

The news boosted Dresdner's shares, already flying high on a string of "buy" recommendations. The stock ended bourse trade up more than three percent at 42.89 marks, after earlier hitting a high for the year of 43 marks.
Dresdner spokesman Bernd Meyer added that the move would not affect the bank's domestic funds business.
"This is merely an integration of units abroad which already exist and which will all remain. German business is not affected at all," Meyer said.
It was not yet clear if the global funds division would be headquartered in San Francisco, where RCM is based, or precisely how its management structure would be organised.
A team of specialists from the three divisions is already working on integrating the units' operations, building on what Dresdner said was already a strong level of co-operation.

Dresdner's Meyer said it was possible that board member Eberstadt, who is in charge of asset management wordwide, could take a direct role with RCM in overseeing the new division but said this would not necessarily be the case.
BHF Bank analyst Dieter Hein said Dresdner would most likely hold back from imposing direct group control on RCM for fear of alienating key executives and losing valuable clients.
"RCM's client base is very important for Dresdner. U.S. pension funds in particular are some of the most important clients in fund management," said Merck Finck's Becker.

RCM, which Dresdner bought last year for $300 million "as a platform for its global money management activities", is one of the leading U.S. asset management firms with around $26 billion under management and 260 blue chip clients.

Kleinwort Benson Investment Management Limited, a unit of Kleinwort Benson Group plc, manages assets of 14.7 billion pounds ($24.23 billion) while Thornton, a specialist equity fund manager based in London and Hong Kong, has more than 1.8 billion pounds in assets under management.
